SUBCONTRACT AGREEMENT

This Subcontract Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into effective as of June 12, 2023 ("Effective Date"), by and between LAKEMONT CONSTRUCTION GROUP, an Illinois corporation, with offices at 1900 Spring Road, Oak Brook, Illinois 60523 ("Contractor"), and MERIDIAN MECHANICAL OF ILLINOIS, LLC, an Illinois limited liability company, with offices at 1455 Busse Road, Elk Grove Village, Illinois 60007 ("Subcontractor").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Contractor is the general contractor for the Naperville Public Library North Branch Renovation project ("Project"), located at 2035 South Washington Street, Naperville, Illinois 60540, for and on behalf of the Naperville Public Library ("Owner"); and

WHEREAS, Contractor desires to engage Subcontractor to perform certain heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and plumbing work on the Project pursuant to the Prime Contract; and

WHEREAS, Subcontractor desires to perform such work, and the parties desire to set forth the terms and conditions governing the performance of such work.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

1. SCOPE OF WORK

1.1 Scope Description. Subcontractor shall perform all labor, materials, equipment, and services necessary to complete all heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and plumbing work (collectively, the "Work") required for the Project, as more particularly described in the Contract Documents and in accordance with the requirements of the Prime Contract. The Work shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards and accepted construction practices.

1.2 Work Included. The scope of the Work includes, but is not limited to, the following:

(a) Design coordination, engineering, fabrication, and delivery of all HVAC systems, including but not limited to: supply and return air ductwork systems, mechanical equipment including chillers, boilers, and air handling units, refrigerant piping, hydronic heating and cooling piping, insulation, vibration isolation, and all controls and monitoring systems. HVAC systems shall include variable air volume and constant volume distribution systems as specified in the Contract Documents.

(b) Design coordination, engineering, fabrication, and installation of all building plumbing systems, including cold and hot water supply systems, sanitary drainage and venting systems, storm drainage systems, natural gas piping, medical gas systems if required, and all fixtures, equipment, and appurtenances as specified in the Contract Documents.

(c) Coordination with mechanical equipment manufacturers for installation support and start-up services.

(d) All labor for rough-in installation, final connection, testing, balancing, flushing, and commissioning of systems to ensure proper operation and Owner acceptance.

(e) System testing, including hydrostatic testing of plumbing and HVAC systems, ductwork pressure testing, and performance verification in accordance with applicable codes and Contract Documents.

(f) Balancing of all air and water systems by certified testing and balancing contractor, included in the Subcontract Price.

(g) Training of Owner personnel in operation and maintenance of all systems prior to Project closeout.

(h) Preparation of accurate as-built drawings reflecting final installation conditions.

(i) Procurement, delivery to jobsite, proper storage, and management of all materials and equipment for the Work.

(j) Temporary facilities, utilities, and services necessary for the Work, including temporary HVAC and water for construction purposes.

(k) All waste management, debris removal, and site cleanup associated with Subcontractor's work area.

1.3 Schedule and Timeline. Subcontractor acknowledges that Final Completion of the Work has occurred on May 15, 2023, and that all systems have been installed, tested, and commissioned. The Warranty Period shall commence upon Final Completion as documented in writing by Contractor and Owner and shall extend through August 31, 2026, as more fully described in Section 8 hereof.

1.4 Quality Standards. All Work shall be performed in strict compliance with the Contract Documents, all applicable building codes (including the International Building Code, National Electrical Code, ASHRAE standards, and applicable local amendments), manufacturer specifications and installation instructions, and all applicable laws and regulations. Subcontractor shall employ only qualified, licensed, and experienced workers for all aspects of the Work.

1.5 Coordination and Means and Methods. Subcontractor shall be responsible for determining and implementing all means, methods, sequencing, and safety measures necessary to perform the Work. Subcontractor shall coordinate all activities with Contractor, the Owner, and other trades to minimize conflicts and ensure proper sequencing. Contractor shall provide overall project coordination and scheduling, and Subcontractor shall comply with all directives regarding coordination and scheduling.

2. PRIME CONTRACT

2.1 Incorporation by Reference. The Contractor's Prime Contract with the Owner, dated March 15, 2023, including all plans, specifications, addenda, change orders, technical specifications, and all other contract documents (collectively, the "Prime Contract"), is incorporated herein by reference and made a part of this Agreement as fully as if set forth herein in their entirety. Subcontractor shall be bound by all terms, conditions, and requirements of the Prime Contract to the extent applicable to the Work performed by Subcontractor.

2.2 Precedence. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the provisions of this Subcontract and the Prime Contract, the following order of precedence shall apply: (1) Prime Contract requirements, (2) this Subcontract, (3) the Contract Documents. To the extent a conflict cannot be reconciled, the more restrictive provision shall apply.

2.3 Prime Contract Review. Subcontractor represents and warrants that it has reviewed the Prime Contract and fully understands all obligations and requirements imposed by the Prime Contract on contractors and subcontractors performing work on the Project.

2.4 Contract Documents Incorporation. All architectural drawings, engineering calculations, equipment schedules, specifications for materials and workmanship, design standards, product data, shop drawings, and industry standards are incorporated herein by reference and shall be binding upon Subcontractor. These include but are not limited to ASHRAE 90.1 energy standards, ASHRAE 62.1 indoor air quality standards, and all applicable plumbing codes and standards.

2.5 Flow-Down of Prime Contract Obligations. To the fullest extent permitted by law, all provisions, covenants, terms, and conditions of the Prime Contract that are applicable to Subcontractor's scope of work, trade, or responsibility are incorporated herein and shall be binding upon Subcontractor with the same force and effect as if Subcontractor were a direct party to the Prime Contract. Contractor shall provide Subcontractor with a copy of the Prime Contract upon request.

2.6 Prime Contract Amendments. If the Prime Contract is amended, modified, or supplemented by written change order or modification, and such amendment impacts Subcontractor's obligations or price, Contractor shall notify Subcontractor in writing within five (5) business days, and such amendments shall be incorporated herein by reference.

3. DEFINITIONS

3.1 "Contract Documents" means the Prime Contract, this Subcontract Agreement, all attached exhibits, all referenced drawings and specifications, all addenda and modifications, and all documents incorporated by reference herein.

3.2 "Project" means the Naperville Public Library North Branch Renovation, a renovation and modernization project of the existing library facility located at 2035 South Washington Street, Naperville, Illinois 60540, including all building systems, site improvements, and related work.

3.3 "Owner" means the Naperville Public Library, a municipal corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of Illinois.

3.4 "Contractor" means Lakemont Construction Group, an Illinois corporation, the general contractor and party to the Prime Contract with Owner.

3.5 "Subcontractor" means Meridian Mechanical of Illinois, LLC, an Illinois limited liability company, the party performing HVAC and plumbing work under this Subcontract.

3.6 "Work" means all labor, materials, equipment, services, and facilities necessary to complete all HVAC and plumbing systems for the Project as described in the Scope of Work.

3.7 "Final Completion" means the date upon which the Work is substantially complete, all deficiencies have been corrected, all systems have been tested and commissioned, and Owner has issued final acceptance, which occurred on May 15, 2023.

3.8 "Warranty Period" means the period commencing on Final Completion and extending through August 31, 2026, a period of approximately two (2) years and three (3) months.

3.9 "Defect" means any failure of the Work to comply with the Contract Documents, any failure of systems to operate as designed and specified, or any deficiency in materials, workmanship, or performance.

3.10 "Change Order" means a written order issued and executed by authorized representatives of both Contractor and Subcontractor authorizing a change in the scope, price, or schedule of the Work.

4. SUBCONTRACT PRICE

4.1 Fixed Lump Sum Price. The total price for the complete performance of all Work under this Subcontract shall be $1,462,000.00 (One Million Four Hundred Sixty-Two Thousand Dollars), payable on a fixed lump sum basis. This price represents full compensation for all labor, materials, equipment, tools, equipment rental, insurance, bonding, overhead, profit, and all other costs and expenses necessary to complete the Work in full compliance with the Contract Documents.

4.2 Price is All-Inclusive. The Subcontract Price is all-inclusive and shall cover all costs including but not limited to: (a) all trades labor for installation, testing, commissioning, and temporary services; (b) all materials, equipment, and products; (c) equipment rentals and temporary facilities; (d) insurance and bonding; (e) payment of prevailing wages and fringe benefits as required by law; (f) traffic control and site management; (g) demolition and removal of existing systems as required; (h) all permits and fees; (i) training and documentation; and (j) all other direct and indirect costs.

4.3 Fixed Price Commitment. The Subcontract Price is fixed and shall not be subject to adjustment, escalation, or increase except as explicitly provided in Section 4.4 or as authorized by written Change Order executed by both parties prior to performing the changed work.

4.4 Limited Exceptions to Fixed Price. The only exceptions to the fixed Subcontract Price shall be:

(a) Changes to the scope of Work as authorized and documented by written Change Order signed by authorized representatives of both parties, with the Change Order specifying the scope change, adjustment to price, and adjustment to schedule if any;

(b) Changes mandated by written direction of Owner or Contractor that expand or alter the Work beyond the original scope as reflected in the Contract Documents;

(c) Changes required by amendments to applicable building codes, design standards, or laws enacted after the Effective Date of this Subcontract that impose new requirements on the Work;

(d) Adjustments to prevailing wage rates as required by the Illinois Prevailing Wage Act and as provided in Section 7 hereof, which shall be limited to increases in the prevailing wage rates published by the Illinois Department of Labor and adjustments shall be made only upon presentation of certified documentation of the new rates; and

(e) No other adjustments, escalations, or additional costs shall be permitted absent a written Change Order.

4.5 Risk of Pricing. Subcontractor assumes all risk with respect to the accuracy of its pricing, market conditions, material cost fluctuations as of the Effective Date, labor availability, and unforeseen site conditions within the scope of typical construction projects. Subcontractor's pricing shall include reasonable contingencies for normal construction conditions and minor obstacles.

5. PAYMENT

5.1 Conditional Payment Terms. Contractor shall pay Subcontractor for the Work completed in accordance with the Contract Documents and this Agreement within thirty (30) days after the later of: (a) receipt of an invoice from Subcontractor, and (b) receipt of payment from Owner for the Work. Payment by Owner to Contractor is a condition precedent to Contractor's obligation to pay Subcontractor. Contractor shall pass through to Subcontractor any payment delays from Owner without prejudice to Subcontractor's warranty obligations.

5.2 Monthly Invoicing. Subcontractor shall submit monthly invoices to Contractor documenting: (a) the percentage of work completed during the invoice period; (b) the cumulative percentage of work completed to date; (c) the amount earned based on the percentage of completion; (c) a description of work performed; (d) materials delivered to the site; (e) any subcontractor and supplier costs incurred; and (f) certification of compliance with prevailing wage and insurance requirements.

5.3 Supporting Documentation. Each invoice shall be accompanied by: (a) evidence of payment of prevailing wages as required in Section 7; (b) certification by Subcontractor that all invoiced work complies with specifications and is properly installed; (c) evidence that all insurance requirements remain in effect; (d) evidence of payment to suppliers and subcontractors if requested; and (e) any other documentation reasonably requested by Contractor.

5.4 Retainage. Contractor shall withhold five percent (5%) of the contract price as retainage from each invoice. The retainage amount shall be held until after Final Completion, correction of all punch list and warranty defects, and written acceptance by Owner. Final retainage shall be released within thirty (30) days after Final Completion and correction of all deficiencies, provided that all warranties remain in effect and Subcontractor provides evidence of correction of all identified defects.

5.5 No Waiver of Rights. Payment of invoices or retainage shall not constitute acceptance of the Work, shall not waive any defects or deficiencies, shall not waive any requirement for correction of non-conforming work, and shall not waive any other rights or remedies of Contractor or Owner. Contractor expressly reserves all rights to require correction of deficiencies at any time during the Warranty Period.

5.6 Insurance Condition Precedent. Contractor shall not be obligated to make any payment to Subcontractor unless Subcontractor maintains current and valid workers' compensation insurance, general liability insurance, and all other insurance required under Section 9, with current Certificates of Insurance provided to Contractor.

5.7 Default Condition. If Subcontractor fails to comply with any material term or condition of this Agreement, including but not limited to prevailing wage requirements, insurance requirements, scope compliance, or schedule requirements, Contractor shall have no obligation to make payment and may pursue remedies for default, including recovery of any costs incurred to complete the Work or correct deficiencies.

5.8 Right to Set Off. Contractor shall have the right to set off against payments due to Subcontractor any costs incurred by Contractor to correct deficiencies, complete the Work, or pursue remedies for Subcontractor's default or breach.

6. PREVAILING WAGE

6.1 Applicability. The Project is subject to the Illinois Prevailing Wage Act (IPWA), 820 ILCS 130/1 et seq., because the Project involves construction on a public works project for the Naperville Public Library, a municipal corporation. Subcontractor acknowledges this requirement and agrees to comply fully and completely with all provisions of the IPWA and all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

6.2 Prevailing Wage Rates. Subcontractor shall pay all employees engaged in the performance of the Work not less than the prevailing wages established by the Illinois Department of Labor for the County in which the Project is located. Current prevailing wage rates for the County of DuPage, effective as of June 2023, for workers engaged in HVAC and plumbing work on public works projects are as follows:

(a) Plumber: $68.50 per hour (including $8.50 fringe benefits)
(b) Pipefitter: $67.25 per hour (including $8.00 fringe benefits)
(c) Sheet Metal Worker (HVAC): $62.75 per hour (including $7.75 fringe benefits)
(d) HVAC Technician: $62.75 per hour (including $7.75 fringe benefits)
(e) Apprentice (3rd Year and Above): $45.00 per hour (including $5.50 fringe benefits)
(f) Laborer (Mechanical): $48.75 per hour (including $6.25 fringe benefits)

These rates include both base hourly wages and fringe benefits paid to employees or into employee benefit funds as required by the IPWA.

6.3 Rate Adjustments. The prevailing wage rates are subject to adjustment by the Department of Labor. Upon receipt of written notice of any increase in prevailing wage rates, Subcontractor shall immediately increase wages for all affected workers, and any resulting increase in cost shall be reflected in Change Order modifications to the Subcontract Price, payable as a cost adjustment without limitation.

6.4 Certified Payroll. Subcontractor shall submit certified payroll reports to Contractor on a weekly basis in accordance with IPWA requirements and Owner requirements. Each payroll report shall be signed under penalty of perjury as required by 820 ILCS 130/2.1 and shall include the following information for each employee: (a) full name and address; (b) Social Security number; (c) job classification; (d) hours worked each day; (e) total hours worked; (f) gross wages and deductions; (g) net wages paid; and (h) confirmation that prevailing wages have been paid in full.

6.5 Payroll Records. Subcontractor shall maintain complete and accurate payroll records for all employees, including time cards, records of wages paid, and records of fringe benefit payments or contributions. Subcontractor shall retain all payroll records for not less than seven (7) years after completion of the Project and shall make such records available for inspection by Contractor, the Owner, or authorized representatives of the Department of Labor upon request, including inspection during normal business hours without advance notice as permitted by law.

6.6 Worker Certification. Subcontractor represents and warrants that: (a) all workers performing the Work are properly classified as to trade, skill level, and experience rating as specified in the IPWA wage determination; (b) all prevailing wages and fringe benefits are being paid in full and on time; (c) no deductions are made from wages except those authorized by law; and (d) Subcontractor is in full compliance with the IPWA.

6.7 Indemnification for Prevailing Wage Violations. Subcontractor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Contractor and Owner from any and all claims, liens, damages, penalties, assessments, interest, attorney fees, and other liabilities arising from Subcontractor's failure to comply with prevailing wage requirements, including but not limited to: (a) any liens filed by employees or the Department of Labor; (b) any claims by employees for unpaid prevailing wages; (c) any penalties assessed by the Department of Labor; (d) any costs incurred by Contractor or Owner to audit Subcontractor's payroll records; and (e) any costs to correct payroll violations or disputes.

6.9 Audit Rights. Contractor and the Owner reserve the right to audit Subcontractor's payroll records and certified payroll submissions at any time during the Project and for three (3) years after Final Completion. If any audit reveals violations of prevailing wage requirements, the cost of the audit and any costs to correct violations shall be deducted from amounts due to Subcontractor.

7. WARRANTY

7.1 Warranty of Quality. Subcontractor warrants that all Work shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, in strict accordance with the Contract Documents, industry standards, and all applicable codes and standards, and that all work shall be of the highest quality consistent with the Project's design and specifications.

7.2 Warranty Period Duration. Subcontractor shall warrant all Work, materials, equipment, and installation for a period of two (2) years from the date of Final Completion, extending through August 31, 2026 (the "Warranty Period"). This warranty period is absolute and shall not be shortened by passage of time, changes in circumstances, or any other factor. The Warranty Period shall commence on May 15, 2023, the date of Final Completion.

7.3 Warranty Coverage. Subcontractor's warranty shall cover:

(a) All HVAC equipment including compressors, motors, fans, controls, thermostats, valves, and all other mechanical and electrical components;

(b) All plumbing equipment and fixtures including faucets, valves, drains, water heaters, pumps, and all other components;

(c) All ductwork, piping, and system distribution components;

(d) All workmanship including installation, connections, testing, balancing, and commissioning;

(e) Proper operation and performance of all systems in accordance with specifications and manufacturers' specifications;

(f) All sealants, insulation, and protective coatings;

(g) The absence of any leaks, failures, or defects in any system component.

7.4 Manufacturer Warranties and Guarantees. Subcontractor shall provide to Contractor and Owner all manufacturer warranties, guarantees, extended warranties, and performance guarantees on equipment and materials supplied. Subcontractor shall transfer and assign such warranties to Owner to the extent permitted by manufacturers and shall execute any documents necessary to effectuate such transfer. Subcontractor shall be responsible for enforcement of warranties against manufacturers and for obtaining warranties for any replacement parts or components.

7.5 Warranty Service Response. During the Warranty Period, Subcontractor shall respond to all warranty calls and requests for corrective action within twenty-four (24) business hours of notification and shall complete all warranty work in a professional and timely manner. Subcontractor shall bear all costs of warranty service, including labor, materials, equipment, and parts. If Subcontractor fails to respond timely, Contractor may arrange for warranty work and deduct costs from amounts due to Subcontractor.

7.6 Commencement of Warranty. The Warranty Period shall not commence until Final Completion as certified by Owner, and the Warranty Period shall not be reduced or eliminated by punch list work, final inspections, or any other final closeout activities. Upon Final Completion and issuance of a Substantial Completion Certificate by Owner, the Warranty Period shall commence as stated herein.

7.7 No Limitation by Statute of Limitations. Subcontractor's warranty obligations shall not be limited or shortened by any statute of limitations, statute of repose, or other legal time limitations that might otherwise apply to contract claims or construction defect claims. The Warranty Period as stated herein shall govern.

7.8 Warranty Survives Acceptance. The warranty shall remain in full force and effect notwithstanding any inspection, acceptance, or payment by Owner or Contractor. Owner's acceptance of the Project or any portion thereof shall not waive or diminish any warranty rights.

7.9 Return to Service. If any system fails or becomes non-functional during the Warranty Period, Subcontractor shall immediately take all action necessary to restore the system to full operation and shall keep the system operational during correction and testing. Any defect in any system shall be corrected at Subcontractor's sole cost and without limitation.

8. INSURANCE

8.1 Types and Limits of Insurance. Subcontractor shall obtain and maintain, at its sole cost and expense, the following insurance coverage throughout the duration of the Work and continuing for a period of not less than two (2) years after Final Completion:

(a) Workers' Compensation Insurance with limits as required by the laws of the State of Illinois, and Employer's Liability Insurance with minimum limits of $500,000 per occurrence for bodily injury by accident, $500,000 per employee for bodily injury by disease, and $500,000 for bodily injury by disease/policy limit;

(b) Commercial General Liability Insurance issued on an occurrence basis (not claims-made) with minimum limits of $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 general aggregate, covering bodily injury, property damage, products/completed operations, and personal injury;

(c) Commercial Automobile Liability Insurance covering all owned, non-owned, and hired motor vehicles used in connection with this Project, with minimum limits of $300,000 per occurrence for bodily injury and property damage combined;

(d) Equipment Insurance covering all tools, equipment, and machinery owned by Subcontractor with values exceeding $5,000.

8.2 Insurer Requirements. All insurance shall be written by insurers rated A:VII or better in the most recent A.M. Best's Insurance Guide and licensed to do business in the State of Illinois. The insurers shall be approved by Contractor prior to commencement of any work.

8.3 Additional Insured. Contractor shall be named as an additional insured on all liability policies (General Liability, Commercial Auto, and Umbrella) on an endorsement basis providing primary and non-contributory coverage with respect to Contractor and its officers, directors, employees, and agents. The Additional Insured endorsement shall be on the ISO form CG 20 10 or equivalent, issued by the insurer, and shall provide coverage for claims arising out of Subcontractor's performance of the Work.

8.4 Owner as Additional Insured. The Naperville Public Library (Owner) shall be named as an additional insured on the General Liability policy for claims arising out of Subcontractor's performance of the Work.

8.5 Certificates of Insurance. Subcontractor shall provide to Contractor, prior to commencing any work on the Project, Certificates of Insurance evidencing all required coverage. The Certificates shall evidence that all policies are in force, that Contractor is named as an additional insured, and that coverage shall not be cancelled, modified, or reduced without thirty (30) days' written notice to Contractor. Certificates shall be renewed at least thirty (30) days prior to expiration of any policy.

8.6 Insurance Maintenance. Subcontractor shall maintain all required insurance continuously throughout the duration of the Work and thereafter as required herein. Failure to maintain insurance shall be grounds for immediate termination of this Subcontract.

8.7 No Waiver of Insurance. The requirement to maintain insurance shall not be waived or reduced by any payment, inspection, or acceptance of the Work, and shall remain in full force during the Warranty Period.

8.8 Contractor's Right to Obtain Insurance. If Subcontractor fails or refuses to maintain any required insurance, Contractor shall have the right, at Contractor's sole option and without obligation, to obtain such insurance at Subcontractor's expense. All costs incurred by Contractor to obtain insurance on behalf of Subcontractor shall be deducted from amounts due to Subcontractor, and Subcontractor shall reimburse Contractor within thirty (30) days of invoicing.

8.9 Waiver of Subrogation. Subcontractor hereby waives any right of subrogation or recovery against Contractor, the Owner, and their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents with respect to any loss, damage, or injury covered by insurance required under this Section, regardless of whether such loss is covered by insurance.

9. INDEMNIFICATION

9.1 Scope of Indemnification. TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY THE LAWS OF THE STATE OF ILLINOIS, INCLUDING THE ILLINOIS COMPARATIVE FAULT ACT (740 ILCS 100/1 et seq.), SUBCONTRACTOR SHALL INDEMNIFY, DEFEND (AT SUBCONTRACTOR'S SOLE EXPENSE USING LEGAL COUNSEL REASONABLY ACCEPTABLE TO CONTRACTOR), AND HOLD HARMLESS CONTRACTOR, ITS PARENT AND AFFILIATE CORPORATIONS, AND THEIR RESPECTIVE OFFICERS, DIRECTORS, EMPLOYEES, AGENTS, AND REPRESENTATIVES FROM AND AGAINST ALL CLAIMS, DAMAGES, LOSSES, LIABILITIES, COSTS, AND EXPENSES, INCLUDING REASONABLE ATTORNEYS' FEES AND LITIGATION COSTS, ARISING OUT OF OR RESULTING FROM:

(a) Subcontractor's performance, non-performance, negligent performance, or defective performance of the Work;

(b) Bodily injury (including death), property damage, or economic loss caused or contributed to by Subcontractor, its employees, agents, or anyone else for whom Subcontractor is responsible;

(c) Violation of any federal, state, or local law, ordinance, rule, or regulation by Subcontractor;

(d) Defects in the Work, including defective materials, equipment, workmanship, or design provided by Subcontractor;

(e) Liens, claims, encumbrances, or stop notices filed by Subcontractor, its suppliers, equipment lessors, employees, or lenders;

(f) Subcontractor's failure to comply with prevailing wage requirements, labor laws, safety laws, or other legal requirements;

(g) Environmental contamination or hazardous materials violations caused by Subcontractor;

(h) Damage to Owner's property, adjacent properties, or public property caused by Subcontractor;

(i) Any claims by third parties arising from Subcontractor's activities.

9.2 Standard of Liability. The indemnification obligation shall apply regardless of whether the claim arises in whole or in part from the negligence, comparative negligence, or contributory negligence of Contractor or Owner, except to the extent that the claim is caused solely by the gross negligence or willful misconduct of Contractor or Owner. Subcontractor shall indemnify and defend Contractor even if Contractor is partially at fault.

9.3 No Limitation by Insurance. The indemnification obligations of Subcontractor shall not be limited by the amount of insurance carried or the amount of insurance proceeds recovered, and shall not be limited by any other provision of this Agreement.

9.4 Defense by Subcontractor. Subcontractor shall defend Contractor against all claims subject to indemnification herein using legal counsel approved by Contractor, at Subcontractor's sole cost and expense. Subcontractor shall conduct all defense and settlement negotiations and shall not settle any claim without Contractor's prior written consent.

9.5 Additional Indemnity. Subcontractor's indemnification obligations under this Section are in addition to and not limited by any insurance requirements or other provisions hereof.

10. TERMINATION

10.1 Termination for Cause. Contractor may terminate this Subcontract immediately upon written notice to Subcontractor if any of the following occur:

(a) Subcontractor fails or refuses to maintain the insurance required by Section 8;

(b) Subcontractor abandons the Work or ceases work for five (5) consecutive business days without authorization or reasonable cause;

(c) Subcontractor fails to pay prevailing wages or fails to submit certified payroll as required by Section 7;

(d) Subcontractor fails to comply with schedule requirements and does not cure such failure within five (5) business days of written notice;

(e) Subcontractor fails to perform the Work in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with the Contract Documents and does not cure such failure within ten (10) business days of written notice;

(f) Subcontractor becomes insolvent or files for bankruptcy protection.

10.2 Completion After Termination. Upon termination for cause, Contractor may complete the Work using other contractors, and Contractor may assess against Subcontractor all excess costs incurred, including all labor, materials, equipment, overhead, and profit charges of replacement contractors.

10.3 Termination for Convenience. Contractor may terminate this Subcontract for convenience without cause upon thirty (30) days' written notice to Subcontractor. Upon termination for convenience, Subcontractor shall be compensated for all work properly completed as of the termination date, less retainage and any deductions for deficiencies, plus reasonable demobilization and equipment removal costs, but shall not be entitled to lost profits or other consequential damages.

10.4 Cessation of Work Upon Termination. Upon termination for any reason, Subcontractor shall immediately cease all work, remove all equipment and personnel from the worksite, and leave the worksite and all areas occupied by Subcontractor in a safe, clean, and secure condition. Failure to remove equipment or materials may result in such removal at Subcontractor's expense.

11. COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS

11.1 Legal Compliance. Subcontractor shall comply fully and completely with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, statutes, ordinances, rules, regulations, orders, and requirements applicable to the performance of the Work, including:

(a) All building codes, electrical codes, plumbing codes, mechanical codes, fire codes, and zoning ordinances;

(b) Illinois Prevailing Wage Act and all prevailing wage requirements;

(c) Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA) and Illinois occupational safety and health laws;

(d) Environmental protection laws and regulations;

(e) Illinois Department of Labor laws and regulations;

(f) Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and accessibility requirements;

(g) All licensing and certification requirements for plumbers, electricians, and HVAC technicians;

(h) Payment of all applicable sales taxes, use taxes, and employment taxes;

(i) All wage and hour laws.

11.2 Licenses and Certifications. Subcontractor represents and warrants that it and all of its employees are duly licensed to perform plumbing and HVAC work in the State of Illinois and hold all required licenses, certifications, and permits. Subcontractor shall provide evidence of such licenses upon request by Contractor.

11.3 Permits and Fees. Subcontractor shall be responsible for obtaining and paying for all permits required for its work, unless otherwise specified in the Prime Contract. Subcontractor shall cooperate with building department inspectors and shall correct any violations noted during inspections.

11.4 Non-Discrimination. Subcontractor shall not discriminate in employment or in the performance of the Work based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, or other protected characteristics. Subcontractor shall comply with all federal, state, and local equal employment opportunity laws and non-discrimination laws.

12. RELATIONSHIP OF PARTIES

12.1 Independent Contractor. Subcontractor is an independent contractor and is not an employee, agent, or representative of Contractor or Owner. Subcontractor is not authorized to act as an agent or representative of Contractor or Owner and shall not represent itself as such to any third party.

12.2 Employment Responsibility. Subcontractor shall be solely responsible for all payroll and employment-related obligations for its employees, including payment of wages, payroll taxes, unemployment insurance, workers' compensation insurance, and all other employment-related costs and obligations.

12.3 Direction and Supervision. While Contractor shall provide general direction as to coordination and scheduling, Subcontractor shall be responsible for all means, methods, sequencing, and safety measures for the Work. Contractor's supervision and inspection shall not relieve Subcontractor of any obligations or constitute acceptance of the Work.

12.4 Authority. Subcontractor has no authority to enter into agreements on behalf of Contractor or Owner or to commit either party to any financial or legal obligations.

13. CHANGES TO THE WORK

13.1 Change Order Requirement. No changes to the scope, schedule, or price of the Work shall be undertaken or performed unless and until a written Change Order has been properly executed by authorized representatives of both Contractor and Subcontractor. Subcontractor shall not begin any changed work until receipt of a fully executed Change Order.

13.2 Change Order Contents. Each Change Order shall specify: (a) a detailed description of the change in scope; (b) the reason for the change; (c) the adjustment to the Subcontract Price, if any; (d) the adjustment to the schedule, if any; (e) the date of authorization; and (f) signature approval by both parties.

13.3 Request for Change Order. Subcontractor shall submit requests for Change Orders within ten (10) business days of first becoming aware of the need for a change. Failure to timely submit a request may result in waiver of any claim for additional compensation or time.

14.1 Right to Inspect. Contractor and Owner shall have the right to inspect all Work at any time during performance and throughout the Warranty Period. Subcontractor shall provide reasonable access and assistance for inspections and shall not impede or delay inspections.

15. COMPLIANCE WITH IMMIGRATION LAW

15.1 IRCA Requirements. The Immigration and Nationality Act as amended by the Immigration Reform and Control Act of 1986 (IRCA) makes it illegal for employers to knowingly hire persons who are not authorized to work in the United States. For all employees, employers are required to complete an Employment Eligibility Verification (Form I-9) which requires the prospective employee to produce documentation that establishes identity and employment eligibility. For additional information, visit www.uscis.gov or consult with an attorney. Subcontractor is solely and exclusively responsible for completing and maintaining Form I-9 for all of its employees.

15.2 IRCA Compliance Representation. Subcontractor represents and warrants that: (a) it is aware of and understands the requirements of IRCA; (b) it is in full compliance with IRCA; (c) it will not knowingly employ or permit to work any person who is not authorized to work in the United States; and (d) it will not employ any worker under this Agreement unless a properly completed Form I-9 has been completed and is on file.

15.3 Verification and Remedial Action. Subcontractor agrees that if it acquires actual or constructive knowledge that one of its employees working on the Project may not be authorized to work in the United States, despite Subcontractor having conducted a facially valid I-9 verification, Subcontractor shall exercise due diligence as required by law to confirm the employee's authorization status and shall take appropriate action, including immediate suspension from the Project and termination of employment if the employee's authorization status cannot be verified.
